title: Almost-linear triangle detection
formal: Does one uniform classical randomized word-RAM algorithm exist that, for every finite simple undirected graph with \(n\) vertices and \(m\) edges given by explicit adjacency lists, returns whether a triangle exists with probability at least \(2/3\), while every execution takes at most \((n+m+2)^{1+o(1)}\) word instructions? The running-time guarantee must cover all graph densities, all valid adjacency-list orders and every random tape.
definitions:
Let \(n\ge0\), \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let \(E\) be a set of unordered pairs of distinct elements of \(V\). Set \(m=|E|\). There are no loops or multiple edges. A triangle is a set \(\{u,v,z\}\) of three distinct vertices for which all three pairs are edges. The output is YES exactly when such a set exists, and NO otherwise; the algorithm need not output a witness or list triangles.

The input supplies \(n,m\), an array of \(n+1\) list offsets, and a contiguous array of \(2m\) vertex labels. The segment for vertex \(v\) contains precisely its neighbors, in an arbitrary order. Each undirected edge occurs once in each endpoint's list. Validity of this representation is promised. Vertex labels, counts and offsets occupy single words. Thus the input occupies \(O(n+m+1)\) words. Disconnected graphs and isolated vertices are allowed; graphs with fewer than three vertices are legitimate NO-instances.

The word length is
\[
 w=\left\lceil4\log_2(n+2)\right\rceil.
\]
Memory consists of addressable \(w\)-bit words; addresses are unsigned words. Input is initially stored in its specified arrays, and other memory is initially zero. A fixed finite program may read or write one addressed word, copy a word, compare unsigned words, branch, perform bitwise Boolean operations, shift logically, add, subtract or multiply modulo \(2^w\), or take the integer quotient and remainder of unsigned division by a nonzero word, at unit cost per instruction. A shift by at least \(w\) positions returns zero. It may also obtain one independent uniform \(w\)-bit random word in one instruction. Longer integers and algebraic operations must be implemented using these instructions. There is no unit-cost arbitrary-precision arithmetic, matrix-product oracle, input-dependent advice or free precomputed table. All input access and preprocessing count toward time. The fixed word length permits the explicit graph representation at every \(n\).

Precisely, set \(S=n+m+2\). The algorithm must halt on every valid graph and every random tape. For every real \(\varepsilon>0\), there must be an integer \(S_\varepsilon\) such that, on every valid input with \(S\ge S_\varepsilon\), every execution uses at most \(S^{1+\varepsilon}\) instructions. The same program works for every \(\varepsilon\); it does not receive \(\varepsilon\) as input. This convention absorbs fixed multiplicative constants and defines the displayed almost-linear bound. Thresholds may depend on \(\varepsilon\) and the program, but not on the graph, its list order or the random tape.

For each fixed input separately, the probability over internal random words of a correct YES/NO output must be at least \(2/3\). There is no average-case input distribution, degree bound, forbidden-subgraph promise, triangle-count promise or restriction to combinatorial methods. Algebraic algorithms are allowed with their actual implementation cost. A deterministic algorithm is allowed as a special case.
answer_criterion:
Give a complete Lean-checked construction and proof of an algorithm satisfying the exact uniformity, word model, all-input time and per-input probability guarantees; or give a complete Lean-checked proof that no such algorithm exists in this model.

A bound with any fixed exponent greater than one is insufficient. A quadratic bound in \(n\) alone need not be almost linear on sparse inputs. Restricted graph classes, counting or listing results, average-case guarantees, and conditional lower bounds do not settle the target by themselves. An expected-time or high-probability-time result needs a proved conversion to the stated all-tapes bound and success guarantee. A separate program for each exponent slack requires a justified uniform combination. The negation of this target need not supply one common positive exponent gap against every algorithm. No numerical approximation tolerance applies to the decision.
why: Determine whether detecting the simplest cyclic graph pattern requires a superlinear amount of computation beyond reading the input.

importance.reason: A fundamental graph primitive and fine-grained hardness assumption with consequences for dynamic data structures, joins and string matching.

status_note: Current status is uncertain: Duan–Zhang arXiv:2509.03215v1 claims a directly relevant near-linear high-probability algorithm, but the displayed amplification inference in §7 does not establish its claimed decaying error and no full proof or corrected implementation has been verified here. The old parent-edge proposal has a checked counterexample, the 2024 proposal is withdrawn, and the September 2026 Aegypti replacement has a different claimed bound. Bounded primary-source checks through 17 September 2026 do not justify either declaring a resolution or asserting unqualified present openness.

context_blocks.text: The output is only one bit. The large number of triangles in a dense graph therefore creates no output-size lower bound for this question. Correctly rejecting graphs with no triangle remains part of the requirement.

The classical sparse bound has exponent \(2\tau/(\tau+1)\) in the edge count for an available matrix-multiplication exponent \(\tau\), plus input reading. This is an upper bound, not a proof that a better unrestricted algorithm is impossible.

Arboricity-sensitive listing takes \(O(m\,a(G))\) time, apart from reading isolated vertices, where \(a(G)\) is the minimum number of forests covering the edges. Bounded arboricity gives useful special cases but is not promised here.
The 2026 weighted improvement and restricted-graph dichotomies answer related questions. They do not supply the required almost-linear algorithm on every explicit graph.

The local-sketching preprint claims \(O(m\log^2 n)\) time and high-probability correctness. Its displayed amplification step in §7 equates \(\exp(-\theta c_G/c_T)\), for positive absolute constants, with \(n^{-\Omega(1)}\). The former is constant, so that inference does not establish the stated decay. This limited check is not a proof that no repair is possible; the claim remains unverified here.
The 2024 combinatorial proposal was withdrawn after an invalid case analysis was identified. It is not an established upper bound.

The older parent-edge rule fails on the path \(0,1,2,3,4,5,6\) with added edges \(\{0,3\},\{3,6\},\{0,6\}\). Its only triangle uses none of the path’s DFS tree edges. This counterexample concerns the stated 2025 rule, not every subsequent implementation.

The replacement posted on 14 September 2026 claims an expected \(O(n^{2.5}\log n)\) dense bound with separate sparse processing. Even a verified result at that bound would not provide the target all-density almost-linear guarantee; its proof was not independently certified.

sentences: The input is an explicit undirected graph, and the output says whether three distinct vertices are pairwise adjacent.
One fixed randomized program must work on every graph and every adjacency-list order.
Every execution must take almost linear time in the number of vertices plus edges, with a correct answer on each input with probability at least two thirds.
A relevant local-sketching preprint remains unverified, so the card records current status as uncertain.
A complete Lean-checked answer must supply this algorithm and its guarantees or prove that none exists in the specified model.

source_formulation.text: Abboud and Vassilevska Williams ask about linear-time triangle detection and state Conjecture 4 as a positive power lower bound in the number of edges on a logarithmic-word RAM. This card retains the existing precise positive target of a single almost-linear algorithm, charges isolated-vertex input explicitly, and fixes worst-case time over its random tapes. Its negation is not identified with the source’s stronger common-exponent lower-bound conjecture.

checked_sources: Read Abboud–Vassilevska Williams, arXiv:1402.0054v1, 1 February 2014, Conjecture 4: common positive delta, expected lower bound in edge count on logarithmic-word RAM. The card retains its existing one-algorithm, worst-case-tape, all-density positive target; its negation is not silently equated with the stronger source conjecture.

Read Alon–Yuster–Zwick, Finding and Counting Given Length Cycles, author PDF introduction pp. 1–3: sparse triangle exponent 2 omega/(omega+1), arboricity/degeneracy comparisons and linear restricted-family bounds. Read the original Chiba–Nishizeki abstract for its O(m a(G)) listing guarantee.

Read Akmal–Fischer, ICALP 2026 Article 10, introduction and Remark 3: node-weighted improvement and distinction between an infimal matrix exponent and an attained runtime. It is not an almost-linear all-density unweighted theorem.

Read the ESA 2026 Article 64 primary abstract, Abboud–Safier–Wallheimer, published 25 August: equivalent dichotomy hypotheses for fixed-pattern-free graph classes, not an unrestricted near-linear algorithm.

Read Duan–Zhang, arXiv:2509.03215v1 of 3 September 2025, abstract, §3 model, §7 pp. 10–11, Theorem 9.1 and proof pp. 13–14, Appendix E parameters. The claimed O(m log² n) high-probability result is directly relevant. In §7 the expression exp(-theta c_G/c_T), with absolute constants, is identified with n^{-Omega(1)}; that expression is a positive constant. This invalidates that displayed inference, not necessarily every possible repair or the entire proposed algorithm. No full proof or artifact audit was performed.
Rechecked Dumitrescu arXiv:2403.01085v2, withdrawal dated 5 March 2024 and author statement that Case 2.1 is invalid.

Read Vega, preprints.org/202506.0875/v3, 19 August 2025, §3 parent-edge rule and completeness proof. Reran the existing finite audit: path 0–1–2–3–4–5–6 plus 0–3, 3–6, 0–6 has the unique triangle {0,3,6}, and no triangle uses a tree edge of the path DFS. The audit concerns the stated rule, not all later implementations.

Read Vega, preprints.org/202511.2197/v11, submitted 9 September and posted 14 September 2026, abstract and Theorem 3: claimed expected O(n^{2.5} log n) dense bound with a separate sparse branch. This is a replacement for the v10 O(n²) claim and is not an almost-linear all-density guarantee; its correctness is not adjudicated.

Bounded primary checks through 2026-09-17 found no independently verified resolution. The relevant unverified local-sketching claim warrants uncertain status rather than an unqualified assertion of present openness.
